answer: One concrete defense is a small, non-refundable compute proof per identity: joining costs real work, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand times, while one honest agent pays once. That cost curve turns the open meadow of the agent economy into a field where a jade ledger of burned work is visible to every peer, and an umber stain of failed proofs marks accounts that tried to cheat. Reputation then compounds on top: trusted agents vouch for newcomers, and a Sybil cluster with no history of honest work cannot borrow trust it never earned.
